title: Verbi Riflessivi
subtitle: Actions you do to yourself — and why their passato prossimo always uses essere.
objectives: Use reflexive pronouns (mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si) with reflexive verbs
Conjugate common reflexive verbs in the present tense
Form the passato prossimo of reflexive verbs, always with essere

content.intro: Italian uses reflexive verbs far more than English does — routines like waking up, getting dressed, or getting bored are all built with a reflexive pronoun plus the verb.
content.explanation: A reflexive verb's infinitive ends in -si (e.g. alzarsi, to get [oneself] up), and the reflexive pronoun changes to match the subject, placed right before the conjugated verb. Every reflexive verb takes essere in the passato prossimo, with the usual subject agreement on the participle.

rules.heading: a) Common reflexive verbs
rules.body: svegliarsi (to wake up), alzarsi (to get up), lavarsi (to wash oneself), vestirsi (to get dressed), chiamarsi (to be named), sentirsi (to feel), annoiarsi (to get bored), divertirsi (to have fun), arrabbiarsi (to get angry).

rules.heading: b) Position of the pronoun
rules.body: Before a conjugated verb: Mi sveglio alle sette. Attached to an infinitive (dropping the infinitive's final -e): Devo alzarmi presto. (equally correct: Mi devo alzare presto.)

examples.it: Mi sveglio sempre alle sei e mezza.
examples.en: I always wake up at half past six.
Did you have fun at the party? (to a male)
See you tomorrow! (literally: we see each other)

examples.it: I bambini si sono lavati le mani.

commonMistakes.why: Reflexive verbs need both the reflexive pronoun and essere as the auxiliary in the passato prossimo — avere alone is never used.

commonMistakes.wrong: Si è arrabbiato con me. (about a woman)
commonMistakes.why: The participle must agree with the subject's gender, exactly as with any other essere verb.
The pronoun mi must pair with the io verb form, sveglio, not the lui/lei form sveglia.

items.explanation: Reflexive pronoun mi + present tense sveglio.
Reflexive pronoun si + loro form divertono.
Reflexive + essere, agreeing with feminine Maria.
Reflexive verbs need the pronoun and essere, never avere alone.
Feminine plural subject needs the -e participle ending.

summary: Reflexive verbs (infinitive -si) use mi/ti/si/ci/vi/si before the conjugated verb.
Every reflexive verb takes essere in the passato prossimo, with participle agreement.
The pronoun can attach to an infinitive instead: devo alzarmi = mi devo alzare.
